# RunsOn Runner Images

The `Runner Images` workflow builds `qgc-candidate-ubuntu24-x64-*` from the current RunsOn Ubuntu 24
full image. The derived AMI preinstalls QGroundControl's Debian build dependencies and desktop Qt
SDK, plus a CPM source seed generated by configuring the image's source revision. RunsOn selects the newest matching AMI from the AWS account and region that host the RunsOn
stack.

Configure these repository settings before dispatching the workflow:

- Variable `RUNS_ON_AMI_SUBNET_ID`: public subnet used by the temporary Packer instance.
- Variable `AWS_REGION`: optional; defaults to `us-west-2`. It must match the RunsOn stack's region.
- Secret `RUNS_ON_AMI_ROLE_ARN`: OIDC role with the EC2 permissions Packer needs to build and
  register an AMI. Promotion and retention also require `ec2:CopyImage`, `ec2:CreateTags`,
  `ec2:DescribeImages`, `ec2:DescribeInstances`, `ec2:DeregisterImage`, and `ec2:DeleteSnapshot`. The role must create the AMI in the RunsOn stack's AWS account and region.

Roll out the image in this order:

1. Configure the settings above.
2. Dispatch `Runner Images` from the repository's default branch.
3. Wait for both the AMI build and `Smoke Test Ubuntu 24 x64` jobs to pass. The smoke job boots the
   exact candidate AMI ID from the Packer manifest and verifies the preinstalled Qt SDK and core Linux build tools.
4. Set `RUNS_ON_LINUX_BUILDER` to `linux-x64-builder-prebaked`.

Leave `RUNS_ON_LINUX_BUILDER` unset to continue using the standard RunsOn image.
Only after smoke testing succeeds does the workflow copy the candidate to the production
`qgc-runs-on-ubuntu24-x64-*` prefix selected by `.github/runs-on.yml`. A failed candidate
cannot become the production default. Configured upstream repositories rebuild weekly.

Cleanup is restricted to images owned by the AWS account with both `Project=qgroundcontrol`
and `ManagedBy=packer` tags and a QGC image prefix. It keeps the newest three production
images, every image used by a pending/running/stopping/stopped instance, production images
under 30 days old, and candidates under seven days old. It deregisters expired images and
deletes associated snapshots; shared snapshots are retained by EC2. The workflow's dedicated
role must have these permissions before enabling the weekly schedule with the subnet setting.

Windows warm pools are organization-level RunsOn configuration. Copy and review
`windows-warm-pool.example.yml` in the organization's `.github-private` repository, then set this
repository's `RUNS_ON_WINDOWS_POOL` variable to `qgc-windows-x64-builder`. Leave the variable unset
until the pool exists; workflows will continue using the ordinary `windows-x64-builder` runner.

The CPM seed lives separately from job workspaces at `/opt/qgc-sdk/cpm`. Its manifest records the
source commit, dependency fingerprint, size in bytes, and preparation time. The cache action copies
it into an empty job cache only when the fingerprint matches. Restored caches take precedence;
a missing or outdated seed falls back to normal CPM downloads. Each job owns its copy, so it can
update moving dependencies without changing the image seed. The image smoke test requires the
seed manifest and source directory before promotion.
